DOTI PT-116.1 General Traffic Control Procedures (April 2022)
Rule 22.3 — Issuance of Permits by the City Traffic Engineer (2022)

windows.note: Weekday lane/bike closures on arterials/collectors approved only 8:30am-3:30pm or 8:00pm-5:00am (Rule 22.3 §IV.4, verbatim-confirmed).

hours.override_note: Sidewalk/bike blockage = lane closure (§III.1). Fees apply daily per day of occupancy (§V.1).

items.label: Residential — street lane
items.note: Rate-table unit basis not recorded in the corpus; fees apply daily per day of occupancy (Rule 22.3 §V.1).

items.label: Collector & Arterial NON-PEAK — 1st lane and parking lane
Collector & Arterial NON-PEAK — 2nd lane
items.note: The escalator is NOT a multiplier: each lane has its own rate; two lanes = $0.45 + $0.90.

items.label: Collector & Arterial PEAK — 1st lane and parking lane
Collector & Arterial PEAK — 3rd lane
items.note: ANOMALY — preserve, do not smooth: the 3rd lane is MORE expensive non-peak ($2.70) than peak ($2.00); so are the 4th-6th at some tiers ($3.00/$4.50/$6.75 peak). It is what the schedule says. Do not normalize.

items.label: Bike lane closure (residential / collector-arterial)
items.note: Two fees that stack: $0.33 bike-lane rate PLUS the $0.45 (non-peak) / $0.50 (peak) lane fee — verbatim 'Bike Lane closure (plus $.45 lane fee)'. Not competing values.

items.label: Expedite (permit requested in a non-standard timeframe)

fees.note: STALENESS RISK: this is the 2024 schedule; Denver publishes annually — 2025/2026 schedules almost certainly exist. Rate depends on road class x geographic zone (Residential / CBD-CCA / Collector-Arterial) x peak flag, with a per-lane escalator that is not a multiplier.

meters.note: TCP 'denied for accuracy or compliance with the MUTCD': Permit Fee + $100 each.
Unauthorized sidewalk/street/alley closure, or reinstatement of a revoked permit: Permit Fee + $500 per day per violation.

applied_deltas.rule: Arrow board required if closing one or more lanes — Denver's trigger is >=1 lane (vs. Colorado Springs' 4+-lane roadway rule).
applied_deltas.baseline: arrow board optional per MUTCD for many single-lane closures
applied_deltas.mode_note: Caution mode only, never an arrow or chevron: one lane is closed on a two-lane, two-way road (MUTCD 11th Ed. §6L.06 ¶18, p. 833; CDOT S-630-1 Sheet 2 General Note 26).

personnel.rule: TCP 'must be prepared by a certified Traffic Control Supervisor' (PT-116.1, Permit 116.1); Rule 22.3 §IV.4.c says 'prepared by a certified traffic control company'. Denver's own procedures name the barricade company as the TCP author for arterials, collectors, and large-scale projects; DOTI Permit Operations can provide typical TCPs for most residential areas.
Signalized intersection affected (per the City Traffic Engineer) -> uniformed police at the Permittee's cost.

device.rule: Steel plates: friction coefficient >=0.35, beveled leading/trailing edges or wedges. Bike detour: M4-9c signage at all decision points.

hazard.rule: TCP 'denied for accuracy or compliance with the MUTCD': Permit Fee + $100 each — precisely the failure the tool exists to prevent.

meter.note: TCP 'denied for accuracy or compliance with the MUTCD': Permit Fee + $100 each.

hazard.rule: Unauthorized sidewalk/street/alley closure, or reinstatement of a revoked permit: Permit Fee + $500 per day per violation.

meter.note: Unauthorized sidewalk/street/alley closure, or reinstatement of a revoked permit: Permit Fee + $500 per day per violation.

notes.rule: Denver is entity-gated: Contractor Licensing issues licenses to work in the ROW (720-865-2770), and the Street Occupancy Request Form requires a Contractor's license number.

Fee-design interaction (Rule 22.3 §IV.4.f, §IV.6.b): (1) maintain a temporary PAR or bike facility in the adjacent parking/travel lane -> that lane's closure fee is WAIVED; (2) fail to maintain 5 ft unobstructed width -> charged the FULL LENGTH OF A BLOCK for the sidewalk/bike closure; (3) covered walkway used as a detour with no added crossings -> reduced closure fee. The engine computes exactly the widths that decide this.
Bus stops: temporary relocation/closure requires written approval from BOTH the City Traffic Engineer and RTD; all accommodation costs on the Permittee.

Paid-parking closure -> separate parking meter permit obtained with the RSOP; meter head removal only by Transportation Operations, billed daily. Unauthorized permanent meter removal: fee = (total yearly meter revenue + citation revenue) x 15 — the largest penalty multiplier in the corpus (not renderable as a fixed meter).

Sheet requirements are the deepest in the corpus: the TCP must depict existing conditions (north arrow, speed limit, geometry, markings, lane assignments, curb lines, sidewalks, PAR, all light/utility/signal poles, all posted signage, bus stops, all parking meters and kiosks with counts, tree lawns, racks, drop boxes) plus proposed items and closure math (taper lengths, advance signage with type/placement/distances, arrow board, work zone length AND width, width of reduced travel lanes). Engine values + a site-survey layer.
Conflicting permits: first-submitted, first-served; coordination with existing permits required.

multi_agency.rule: RTD approval for bus-stop changes; ROWS Construction Engineering reviews arterial/collector TCPs; Permit Operations may approve local/residential at the counter.

leads.label: Standard RSOP
leads.note: Published as '>=5 days' (unit as published; Rule 22.3 §IV.1).

notices.rule: Lane / sidewalk / bike closure: notify >=48 hrs. Schools, health care, senior/community centers within 500 ft must be included. All closures: door hanger (area, dates, contractor contact) + posted weather-resistant sign at the closure with RSOP number, duration, contact.
Press release, issued by the Permittee.
